title: The hawk-eyed songbird: retinal morphology, eye shape, and visual fields of an aerial insectivore
why: Tree swallow (Tachycineta bicolor) acuity, binocular field and receptor spacing; the abstract and press page name no numbers. The Dryad dataset (10.5061/dryad.n7140, opened as a landing page only) holds visual-field spreadsheets. DOI of the paper not confirmed.
get: journal via library; open data at https://datadryad.org/dataset/doi:10.5061/dryad.n7140

authors: Moore BA, Tyrrell LP, Kamilar JM, Collin SP, Dominy NJ, Hall MI, Heesy CP, Huynh H, Lisney TJ, Yopak KE, Fernández-Juricic E
title: Does retinal configuration make the head and eyes of foveate birds move? (Appendix 1: the 29 species)
why: Open-access article whose species list and per-species retinal values sit in Appendix 1 (not in the article text I opened). Could hold peak ganglion density, and hence acuity, for Vireo, Catharus, Baeolophus or other songbird genera of this batch.
get: open access: supplementary Appendix 1 PDF from https://doi.org/10.1038/srep38406

authors: Grötzner SR, Rocha FA de F, Corredor VH, Liber AMP, Hamassaki DE, Bonci DMO, Ventura DSF
title: Distribution of rods and cones in the red-eared turtle retina (Trachemys scripta elegans)
why: Rod and cone topography and asymmetry of the red-eared slider retina; the repository page lists keywords (retina, photoreceptors, colour vision, binocular vision, asymmetry) but no values. Would give the sharp-vision region and cone density for Trachemys.

authors: Fernández-Juricic E, Gall MD, Dolan T, O'Rourke C, Thomas S, Lynch JR
title: Visual systems and vigilance behaviour of two ground-foraging avian prey species: white-crowned sparrows and California towhees
why: Acuity, binocular and lateral fields of the California towhee (Melozone crissalis), the only measured member of Melozone. Cited in Moore et al. 2013 and 2015; DOI not confirmed from a page I opened.

authors: Budnik V, Mpodozis J, Varela FJ, Maturana HR
title: Regional specialization of the quail retina: ganglion cell density and oil droplet distribution
why: Ganglion cell density in a quail (the repository page does not name the species; Callipepla californica is the common quail of Chile, so it may be this genus). Would give the sharp-vision region and a basis for acuity in Callipepla.
get: journal via library; the page gives 2018 as an issue date that conflicts with 1984
